mainTopic: Why both פסוקים are needed to exempt an oath to cancel a מצוה; the משנה of נדר בתוך נדר versus שבועה בתוך שבועה; and the מחלוקת between רב הונא and שמואל about a repeated vow of נזירות.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge. The פסוק 'להרע או להיטיב' already teaches that an oath to cancel a מצוה does not take effect, so why do we also need 'לא יחל דברו'? The גמרא answers that each פסוק exempts from something different. One exempts from the קרבן, and the other exempts from the לאו. Then a new משנה teaches that a נדר can take effect on top of a נדר, but a שבועה cannot take effect on top of a שבועה. It shows this with two vows of נזירות and two oaths not to eat. In the גמרא, רב הונא says a second נזירות takes effect only if it adds something, like 'today' and then 'tomorrow.' שמואל says it takes effect even when the words are exactly the same. The גמרא then challenges רב הונא: if he is right, the משנה should have shown the contrast inside נדרים alone, instead of setting נדרים against שבועות. That challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The verse 'to do evil or to do good' already excludes an oath against a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge. The פסוק 'להרע או להיטיב' already teaches that an oath only works on optional things, so an oath to cancel a מצוה is already excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'to do evil or to do good.' Doing good is about something optional, so doing evil must also be about something optional. That leaves out someone who swore to cancel a מצוה, because cancelling a מצוה is not his choice to make.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is completing a challenge that began just before this. Why do we need the פסוק 'לא יחל דברו' to exclude an oath to cancel a מצוה, if 'להרע או להיטיב' already excludes it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts 'doing evil' next to 'doing good.' 'Doing good' means a positive act that a person is free to do or not do. So 'doing evil', which means holding back from something, must also be about something optional. A מצוה is not optional, so an oath to cancel it is already left out, and a second פסוק seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches; the source is the פסוק
To do evil or to do good (ויקרא 5:4)
Optional; something a person is free to choose

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new teaching. It is the end of a question. The גמרא is asking why we need two פסוקים for the same rule.

phrases.english: The verse states: 'to do evil or to do good.'
Just as 'doing good' is about something optional,
so too 'doing evil' is about something optional.
This excludes one who swore to cancel a מצוה
and then did not cancel it,
since the choice is not in his hands!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge begun before this section, which asked why 'לא יחל דברו' is needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the פסוק 'לא יחל דברו' to exclude an oath to cancel a מצוה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'להרע או להיטיב' already limits oaths to optional matters, so a second פסוק adds nothing.

steps.title: Each verse exempts from something different
steps.stepSummary: One פסוק exempts the person from the קרבן of an oath. The other exempts him from the לאו of breaking an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: One פסוק teaches that he does not bring a קרבן for breaking such an oath. The other teaches that he does not break the לאו of oaths.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Both פסוקים are needed because each one removes a different consequence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'להרע או להיטיב' appears in the section about קרבנות, so it exempts him from the קרבן. 'לא יחל דברו' is the commandment not to break your word, so it exempts him from the לאו. Without both, we would only know about one of the two exemptions.

keyTerms.meaning: The offering brought for breaking an oath
The prohibition against breaking an oath

steps.whatToRemember: An oath to cancel a מצוה does not take effect at all. The person is exempt both from the קרבן (from 'להרע או להיטיב') and from the לאו (from 'לא יחל דברו').

phrases.english: One verse is to exempt him
phrases.notes: This is the verse 'להרע או להיטיב,' from the section on קרבנות.

phrases.english: from the offering for an oath,
and one is to exempt him
from the prohibition of an oath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1 by giving each פסוק its own job.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the verses: each covers a different consequence.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both פסוקים seemed to teach the same exemption.
steps.terutzMaskana: One פסוק exempts from the קרבן, and the other exempts from the לאו.

steps.title: The משנה: a vow can stack on a vow, an oath cannot stack on an oath
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens. A second נדר can take effect on top of a first one, but a second שבועה on the same thing does not take effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: There can be a vow inside a vow. But there cannot be an oath inside an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a general rule. It contrasts נדרים with שבועות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a person makes the same נדר twice, both can take effect. If he makes the same שבועה twice, only the first one counts, and the second adds nothing. The משנה will next show examples of each.

keyTerms.meaning: A vow taking effect on top of a vow
An oath taking effect on top of an oath

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule sets up the whole סוגיא that follows, which asks exactly when a second vow really adds something.

phrases.english: MISHNAH
There is a vow within a vow,
but there is no oath within an oath.

steps.triggerLanguage: יֵשׁ נֶדֶר בְּתוֹךְ נֶדֶר, וְאֵין שְׁבוּעָה בְּתוֹךְ שְׁבוּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה, unconnected to the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A second נדר can take effect on a first נדר; a second שבועה cannot take effect on a first שבועה.

steps.title: The משנה's examples: two nazirite vows versus two oaths
steps.stepSummary: The משנה illustrates its rule. Saying twice 'I am a נזיר if I eat' makes him obligated twice. Saying twice 'an oath that I will not eat' makes him liable only once.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If someone says 'I am a נזיר if I eat' two times and then eats, he must keep נזירות for each one. If he says 'I swear I will not eat' two times and then eats, he is liable only once.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers its own question 'כיצד' by giving one example of each half of the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With נזירות, both vows take effect, so he owes two terms of נזירות. With the שבועה, the second oath adds nothing, because he was already bound by the first. So eating breaks only one oath.

phrases.english: How so?
He said: 'I am a nazirite if I eat,'
'I am a nazirite if I eat,' and then he ate:
he is obligated for each and every one.
'An oath that I will not eat,'
'An oath that I will not eat,' and then he ate:
he is liable only once.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives concrete cases for the rule stated in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two conditional נזירות vows both take effect; two identical oaths count as only one.

steps.title: רב הונא: a second נזירות takes effect only if it adds a day
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא limits the משנה. A second נזירות takes effect only when it adds something, such as 'today' and then 'tomorrow.' If both vows say 'today,' the second does not take effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: the משנה is talking only about someone who said 'I am a נזיר today' and then 'I am a נזיר tomorrow.' Because an extra day is added, the second נזירות takes effect. But if he said 'today' and then 'today' again, the second נזירות does not take effect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with רב הונא, who narrows the משנה's rule of 'נדר בתוך נדר' to a case where the second vow adds something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא holds that a second vow works only if it changes something. 'Tomorrow' starts a day later, so it adds an extra day, and that lets the whole second נזירות take hold. Two identical vows of 'today' add nothing, so the second is empty, just like a repeated שבועה.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of...
Since; because of the fact that
The state of being a נזיר

steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא does not reject the משנה. He limits it: 'נדר בתוך נדר' works only when the second vow adds something.

phrases.english: GEMARA
Rav Huna said:
They taught this only where he said
'I am a nazirite today,' 'I am a nazirite tomorrow,'
since an extra day is being added,
phrases.notes: The second vow starts a day later, so it ends a day later. That is the extra day.

phrases.english: naziriteship takes effect upon naziriteship.
But if he said: 'I am a nazirite today,'
'I am a nazirite today,'
naziriteship does not take effect upon naziriteship.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the משנה's rule of 'נדר בתוך נדר' to a specific case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A second נזירות takes effect only if it adds something new, such as an extra day; identical repeated vows of נזירות do not stack.

steps.title: שמואל: even an identical second נזירות takes effect
steps.stepSummary: שמואל disagrees with רב הונא. Even if the person says 'I am a נזיר today' twice, the second נזירות still takes effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: even if he said 'I am a נזיר today' and then 'I am a נזיר today' again, the second נזירות takes effect on him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings שמואל, who argues with רב הונא and reads the משנה without any limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, the second vow does not need to add anything new to take effect. He can keep one term of נזירות after the other, so both vows count. This opens a מחלוקת that the גמרא will go on to discuss.
steps.whatToRemember: There is a מחלוקת. רב הונא says a repeated נזירות counts only if it adds something, like 'tomorrow.' שמואל says it counts even when the words are exactly the same.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
Even if he said: 'I am a nazirite today,'
'I am a nazirite today,'
naziriteship takes effect on him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב הונא's limitation in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even two identical vows of נזירות both take effect.

steps.title: Why didn't the משנה contrast two kinds of vows?
steps.stepSummary: According to רב הונא, the משנה should have taught a contrast inside נדרים: sometimes a second נדר takes effect and sometimes it doesn't. It should not have contrasted נדר with שבועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רב הונא, instead of teaching 'there is no שבועה within a שבועה,' the משנה should have taught: 'There is a נדר within a נדר, and there is no נדר within a נדר.' 'I am a נזיר today, I am a נזיר tomorrow': there is a נדר within a נדר. 'I am a נזיר today,' 'I am a נזיר today': (the sentence finishes on the next amud).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is attacking רב הונא's view from step 5. It says that if he were right, the משנה would have been worded differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא said a second נזירות takes effect only when it adds something new. If so, the משנה could have taught the whole rule inside נדרים alone: one kind of repeated נדר takes effect and one kind doesn't. So why did it bring in שבועות at all? The challenge is only that the wording is strange on רב הונא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it teach; the משנה should have said
And there is no vow within a vow: a case where the second נדר does not take effect

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the משנה is wrong. It is saying that רב הונא's reading makes the משנה's wording strange. The challenge is against רב הונא, not against the משנה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This kind of challenge, 'the משנה should have taught a smaller contrast,' tests whether a limitation fits the wording of the משנה. The answer will decide whether רב הונא's limitation can stand.

phrases.english: And according to Rav Huna,
instead of teaching 'there is no oath within an oath,'
phrases.notes: This is the second half of the משנה from step 3, which set נדר against שבועה.

phrases.english: let it teach: there is a vow within a vow,
and there is no vow within a vow.
'I am hereby a nazir today, I am hereby a nazir tomorrow':
there is a vow within a vow,
'I am hereby a nazir today,' 'I am hereby a nazir today':

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַב הוּנָא, אַדִּתְנָא אֵין שְׁבוּעָה בְּתוֹךְ שְׁבוּעָה, לִיתְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the disagreement between רב הונא and שמואל, the גמרא tests רב הונא's view against the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's limitation that a second נזירות takes effect only when it adds something new (step 5).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If repeated נדרים split into ones that take effect and ones that don't, the משנה should have shown that split inside נדרים. Instead it contrasts נדר with שבועה, which suggests every repeated נדר takes effect.
